verdict.rationale: Slate's docs describe spinning up multiple subagents that run in the background in parallel across several tasks. They appear as a grid of inline cards you can drill into, while you keep planning and queuing work. The docs also claim support for multi-hour sessions, and a --yolo flag removes permission prompts so agents can run unattended. Missing for 10: evidence of runs lasting days rather than hours, documented scale limits or behavior for large fleets, detached/remote execution that survives closing the terminal, and independent or hands-on corroboration of long parallel runs.
